test_input: Press RIGHT for 5 seconds, then UP for 2 seconds, then LEFT for 3 seconds, then DOWN for 2 seconds. Repeat until game over. Press R to restart. Press ESC to quit.
notes:
Play manual for Snake (implementation files: game/snake_game.py, game/snake.py, game/food.py, game/constants.py)

Controls and exact console lines (every control the game handles prints a line when it takes effect):
- Arrow keys (Up/Down/Left/Right): changes direction if not reversing. Console prints: "DIRECTION <DIR>" where <DIR> is one of RIGHT, LEFT, UP, DOWN. No line is printed if the key would reverse the snake.
- R: Restart anytime. Console prints: "RESTART". This resets snake to initial 3-square center, score to 0, and respawns food.
- Escape or window close: Quit. Console prints: "QUIT" and the game exits.

Game events printed to console:
- When the score increases after eating food: "SCORE:<n>" (e.g. SCORE:1). This prints immediately when food is eaten.
- When the game ends due to wall or self collision: "GAME OVER" is printed to the console.

Visible UI and behavior:
- Grid: 20 by 20 cells, rendered as a grid occupying the bottom 600x600 pixels of the 600x680 window. (Top 80 px reserved for UI showing score and controls.)
- Snake: starts as 3 green squares in the center of the grid, moves one square per tick at FPS=10 (one cell per frame). Movement is discrete by grid cell.
- Food: single red square placed at a random empty cell (not overlapping snake). New food spawns immediately after being eaten.
- Eating food: snake grows by one cell and score increases by 1.
- Collisions: If the head moves outside the 20x20 grid or into the snake body (except moving into the tail cell when it moves away in the same tick), the game ends. On game over the snake stops moving and "GAME OVER" and "Final Score: N" are shown on screen.
- Controls text ("Arrows: Move   R: Restart   Esc: Quit") is displayed below the score at the top of the window.

Implementation notes and file responsibilities:
- game/constants.py: grid size, resolution, colors, cell size, UI height, FPS.
- game/snake.py: Snake class; owns positions list, direction, movement, growth, and self-collision check. Methods: reset(), get_positions(), head(), set_direction(dx,dy), move(grow=False), collides_with_self().
- game/food.py: Food class; owns position and spawn(snake_positions) to pick a random empty cell.
- game/snake_game.py: main entry point (entry_point). Owns game loop, score, game_over flag, input handling, rendering, and restart logic. Functions: grid_to_pixel(cell), draw_grid(surface), main().

Limitations and notes:
- No win condition is implemented (game only ends on loss). This matches the Plan which provided no win rule.
- Food placement is random; in extremely rare cases when the snake fills the board, food becomes None (no available cell).
- Graphics are plain colored rectangles (no images or sounds), as required.
- The game prints only the lines described above; it does not print intermediate debug information.

Exact runtime settings:
- Resolution: 600x680, FPS: 10, Grid: 20x20 cells (cell size 30 px), UI height: 80 px.

How to run:
- Run python -m game.snake_game or python game/snake_game.py.
